terms.definition: Dividing a vector by its length, which keeps its direction and makes its length 1.
One frame that takes far longer than the frames around it, so that the motion visibly jumps.
Deciding when each frame may start, so that frames come at a steady rate.
Handing a finished image to the display only when the display starts its next refresh.
The present mode in which finished images wait in a line, first in, first out, and the display takes one at each refresh; the mode that gives vsync.
A highest frame rate that a loop does not exceed.
The list of files and lines that leads from something the reader can see, such as an option, a message or a label, to the code where it acts, each line with a few words on what happens there.
EnTT's container of entity numbers and component storages, of which every scene has one.
A place inside a registry that keeps one object per type for the whole registry, where a module keeps its per-scene state.
A node of a tree, or an entity of a scene, with everything below it: its children, their children and so on.
How much of the light that reaches a surface the surface sends back, and in which directions.
One of the lists of instructions a core keeps in progress at the same time; many x64 cores have two.
One of the few dozen places inside a core where the numbers wait that an instruction works on right now.
A loop that runs one turn too many or too few, usually because < and <= were mixed up.
A list of changes marked for the next commit.
To bring the commits of another branch into the current one.
A clash where both branches changed the same line, which git leaves for the person to settle.
A fixed name for one commit.
A diff saved in a file.
A second working folder of the same repository, with its own branch checked out.
The order of numbers made by mixing the bits of two or three coordinates into one.
The digits of a floating-point number after its leading one.
A float below the smallest one of the usual form, whose leading 1 is dropped.
Removing an array item in constant time by copying the last item into its place and shrinking the array by one.
A list of the unused slot indices of an array, from which the next new item takes its slot.
A running total of a list of counts, giving the place where each group starts in one shared array.
The number of items of a hash map divided by its number of buckets.
A tree in which each node has at most two children, the keys of its left subtree are smaller than its own and those of its right subtree larger.
A map built on a balanced search tree that finds a key in O(log n), lists its keys in order and never moves its nodes.
A queue that gives out the waiting item with the best priority, whatever its arrival time.
A tree stored in an array in which every node is no larger than its children, so the smallest item sits at index 0.
A tree that cuts space into parts so that a search skips every part that cannot hold the answer.
A path of arrows in a directed graph that leads back to its start.
A list of the nodes of a dependency graph in which every node comes after the nodes it needs.
An array in which each item holds the number of a parent, so that two items are in one group when their roots are equal.
A sort that keeps the order of items with equal keys.
What happens when a derived object is copied into a base value: the copy keeps only the base part and loses the derived part and its virtual behavior.
A table, made once per class, that lists the address of each virtual function of that class; a hidden pointer in each object leads to it.
An argument of a template that is a type, as the float of Row<float, 3>.
The object extract returns, which owns one node of a map and lets you change its key before insert.
The address of a plain function, the C form of a callback.
A void* that a C library stores and passes back to the callback.
A plain struct a C library takes its settings in, completed by the caller and passed by pointer.
A value of a type such as float Coin::* that names a field of a class, not of one object.
A type that holds exactly one of several listed types at a time and knows which, as std::variant.
A parameter written Args&&... in a template, which binds to both temporaries and named objects and remembers which, so that std::forward passes it on as it came.
A declaration such as const auto [end, error] = ... that splits a pair or struct into named variables.
A class that is declared (class Scene;) but not yet defined.
A template in <type_traits> that answers a question about a type at compile time, as std::is_same_v.
A name that an object file defines or needs, such as a function.
The one place that makes a declared thing exist, such as a function's body.
The building of a program's global variables before main begins, in an order C++ leaves open between source files.
A named thing to build, such as a library or a program, that carries its own include folders, definitions and links.
The file CMakeCache.txt, where CMake keeps its settings between runs of the configure step.
The compiler rewriting code into machine code that does the same job in less time.
A fixed value at the start of a file that says which format the file claims to be.
The block of fixed size at the start of a file that describes the rest of the file.
The rule that a value starts at an address that is a multiple of a number, usually its type's size.
Unused bytes the compiler inserts between members or after the last one of a struct.
A struct that keeps its members in declaration order, so that offsetof is allowed.
A small part of a document that names its kind and its version, so a reader checks them before it trusts the rest.
The part of a reader that checks that tokens follow the rules of a format and builds the values from them.
A short text that describes a set of texts, so that a program can ask whether a text matches it.
The simple pattern that file names use, such as *.cpp, where * stands for any run of characters.
A hash whose rule is written down and never changes, so every program on every machine gives the same number for the same bytes.
A 3×3 change followed by a move, whose 4×4 matrix has the bottom row 0, 0, 0, 1.
The matrix with rows and columns swapped, so the number in row i and column j moves to row j and column i.
Three vectors of length 1 at right angles to each other; the columns of a rotation form one.
A second direction along a surface, at a right angle to its tangent.
The space whose axes are a surface's tangent, bitangent and normal.
The factor by which a matrix multiplies areas in 2D or volumes in 3D; negative for a mirror, zero for a flat matrix.
The coordinate system whose origin is the camera, with +X to its right, +Y up and -Z straight ahead.
The flat surface at distance 1 in front of the camera, at a right angle to its view direction, on which every point is drawn.
The quaternion with the signs of x, y and z flipped; for a unit quaternion it is the inverse.
The fact that each rotation has exactly two unit quaternions, q and -q.
A vector whose direction is the axis a body turns around and whose length is the rate in radians per second.
The rotation that changes nothing, the quaternion (1, 0, 0, 0).
The distance of a point from a plane, positive on the side the plane's normal points to, negative on the other side and 0 on the plane.
An equation of the form a t squared plus b t plus c equal to 0, solved by the quadratic formula.
A simple shape, a sphere or a box, that holds a complex one and stands in for it in a cheap first test.
The space between two parallel planes; a box is where three slabs meet.
Said of a shape when a straight line between any two of its points stays inside it.
A direction onto which the shadows of two convex shapes do not overlap, which proves that they do not touch.
A blend of the four corner values of a square, made by lerps along x on two edges and then along y between the results.
A quantity that loses the same fraction in each equal step of time or distance.
The time tau = 1 / k after which an exponential decay has fallen to 1 / e, 36.8 %, of its start.
The time an exponential decay needs to lose half its value, ln 2 / k.
A sum in which each term is the one before it times the same number r, with the sum 1 / (1 - r) for 0 < r < 1.
False, wide stripes that appear when a fine regular pattern is sampled too coarsely.
Said of two cases that cannot both happen, so their probabilities add.
Said of a distribution where every value, or every part of a range of the same size, is equally likely.
The average of the squared distances of samples from their mean.
The square root of the variance, in the units of the samples.
Cutting a range into equal cells and putting one random point in each.
The angle between a direction and the up axis: 0 degrees for straight up, 90 for the horizon, 180 for straight down.
The angle around the up axis, measured from +X toward +Z.
A picture whose columns step evenly in azimuth and whose rows step evenly in polar angle.
Finding the weights of a shape's basis functions by multiplying the shape by each pattern and summing.
The rise above the true value on one side of a sharp edge and the fall below it on the other that a cut-off series of basis functions shows, which can make light negative.
A call such as std::atomic_thread_fence that orders the reads and writes around it, in the direction of release or acquire, without an operation on a variable.
A stop-at-once check that ends the program on a programmer error; some engines remove it from the shipped build.
The part of a log message that says how serious it is.
A named source of log messages, which says where a message came from.
A place where log messages end, such as the console or a file.
A failure that real data or a real system can cause, which the program survives by returning an error.
A run whose output is the point: it prints help or a usage error, or runs without a window for a tool, a script or a person at a terminal.
The whole steps still due when the cap stops a frame's loop of fixed steps.
The image that the graphics card draws a window into, whose size GetFramebufferSize gives in pixels.
Several queues in one pool, emptied in order, so that urgent work overtakes work that can wait.
A set of jobs in which each job names the jobs it needs first.
A scheme in which each thread has a queue of its own and a thread without work takes jobs from another thread's queue.
A light stack that a program switches to and from by itself, without the operating system.
A place where two parts of a program meet and one side can change without the other noticing.
The time spent in a stage without the time of the stages nested in it.
Said of a frame whose CPU work takes at least 90 % of the frame interval, so the GPU waits for the CPU.
Said of a frame whose GPU busy time takes at least 90 % of the interval and is longer than the work time, so the CPU waits for the GPU.
Said of frames where neither CPU nor GPU reaches 90 % of the interval, so vsync, a frame-rate cap or idle throttling sets the pace.
The number a LogBuffer gives each entry, one higher than the last and never used twice.
The function that gets a failed assert's condition, file, line and message and answers Break, Abort or Continue.
The set of component types that an entity has.
A steady motion that looks jerky because it is drawn in unequal jumps.
Drawing an entity where its last speed says it should be by now, ahead of the newest simulated pose.
The scene's list of entities that the latest stepping frame moved, with a drawn matrix for each.
The role of an interpolated entry that moved only because an ancestor moved: it is drawn as its parent's drawn matrix times its own local transform.
The role of an interpolated entry drawn where it is, with no blend.
The role of an interpolated entry whose own transform changed in the steps: it is drawn between its world pose before them and after them.
Drawing what the fixed steps moved between its pose before and its pose after the latest steps, so that motion looks smooth at any frame rate.
The stage that finds which pixels a triangle covers, taking each pixel's center as one sample.
How many bytes per second a memory can move.
A single copy of a shader program that the GPU runs on one item of data.
One command that starts a compute shader as many thread groups.
A fixed number of threads that run together on one part of the GPU and can share fast memory.
A small, fast block of memory that all threads of one thread group read and write, and that no other group can see.
A point where every thread of a group waits until all of them reach it, which also makes their shared-memory writes visible.
The upload steps recorded between BeginBatch and SubmitBatch, sent to the GPU in one submission and closed with a fence.
Coordinates that count across an image from 0 to 1 along each side, whatever its size in pixels.
A script that is always in exactly one of a fixed list of named situations, called its states, and that moves from one to another only along rules you write down.
A set of objects built once, up front, and reused instead of created when needed and destroyed after.
A function of a game object that the engine calls once for each frame, in which the object moves itself a little.
A code editor with a build button and name completion.
Bytes that come from outside the running program, which may be cut, damaged by an accident or written to cause harm, so the program checks them before it uses them.
Writing the data first and the note that names the data last, so that a note never points at data that is not there yet.
the parts of a BC7 block encoding.
players choosing controls.
The Audio system's data for one entity: its voice, the component values last applied and the flags of what the game asked for.
The way an audio device asks the mixer for each period of sound on its own thread, instead of the game pushing queued buffers.
A list of drawables built again each frame by walking the scene.
One record per drawable that persists across frames and is updated from change signals.
The retained records kept in GPU memory, from which the GPU builds the draws.
triangular probability density noise.
A counter the renderer raises when earlier exposure readbacks stop describing the frames to come; only readbacks of the current epoch are read.
A full-screen pass over a finished picture, here an anti-aliasing pass.
Two textures that swap roles each frame, the resolve reading one and writing the other.
The same arithmetic as a shader function, written in C++ so that a test can run it without a GPU.
A material that does not conduct electricity, which scatters most light inside it as diffuse color and mirrors a small share.
The exponent of Phong's model that sharpens a highlight as it grows.
The coordinate system of the light's camera, whose view-projection matrix gives a point's place in the shadow map.
A move of the point that reads the shadow map along the surface's normal, away from the surface.
A stored bundle of sky light and sun values in real units, applied by lighting.applySkyPreset.
The sun lighting a scene twice, once from a directional light and once from the environment map.
A float whose bits are changed so that comparing them as unsigned integers orders the floats.
A broad phase that sorts bounding boxes along one axis and compares only boxes whose intervals overlap.
A broad phase that writes each body into the cells of an equal-sized grid and pairs bodies that share a cell.
A binary tree of bounding boxes in which each inner box encloses its children, updated as bodies move.
A bounding box larger than the body's real box by a margin, so that the tree changes only when the real box leaves it.
The narrow-phase test that declares two convex shapes apart when some axis shows a gap between their projections.
The point of a convex shape that lies farthest along a given direction.
The smallest set of points (a point, a segment, a triangle or a pyramid) that GJK keeps as its current guess.
a small range around rest read as zero; axial per axis, radial on the stick's length.
A counter in an animator instance that changes whenever what plays changes: a state, a transition or a clip.
A character turned into physics bodies joined by constraints, so it falls limp.
The animator without a controller: it plays the clip set on the component and runs no state machine.
A session in which a person who has not seen the game plays it while the maker watches and stays silent.
The short cycle of action, result and reward that a player repeats for the whole game.
The amount of game a maker commits to make: its features, its content and its polish.
A list that sorts every feature of a game into must, should and could.
A rough, quick version of a game made to answer one question.
A game built in the engine from plain shapes, with no art.
One small part of a game made to the quality of the finished game.
A few sentences, written before the work, that fix what the player does, the loop, win and loss, the controls and the cuts.
The square a piece's four cells sit in, inside which a quarter turn works.
A small shift that a game tries when a turned piece does not fit.
A collider that follows the triangles of a mesh, allowed only on static bodies.
A script field that holds a reference to an asset, which a pruned export follows.
The camera the person moves to look at the scene while they edit it, which no game contains.
A camera that always looks at one point and turns around it at a fixed distance.
To turn the camera around its target at the same distance, so the object stays in the middle of the view.
A picture of the edited scene that a command renders and returns; it is not a screenshot of the viewport.
The one-time upgrade that reads the scenes of a project of version 1 or 2 and writes the project's collision layer table, so that the project becomes version 3.
The list of projects the launcher shows, at most 12, most recent first, kept in a file of the user's data folder.
The person's own editor settings that hold for every project, kept in Preferences.json in the user's data folder.
The note a script build tree keeps (StrataScriptBuild.json) of the toolchain and settings it was configured with and, after a successful configure, the sorted list of the script folder's files.
One error or warning found in a build log, split into file, line, column, severity, code and message.

One number per thumbnail, a hash of the version, the image size and the handle and content stamp of an asset and everything it depends on; the thumbnail is current while its stored key equals the computed one.
The older darkening of a point that grows with the nearness of blocking surfaces and ignores angles.
A list of light sources ordered from the most exact to the least, each layer taking a weight and passing the remaining share down.
Halving the interval between the last ray point in front of a surface and the first point behind it, keeping the half that holds the crossing.
A texture that holds the light of a scene's surfaces, computed before the game runs.
A written design that names the goal, the starting point, the decisions, the steps, the tests and the acceptance numbers of a change before the change begins.
A line of text in an Inspector section that describes the state of the renderer or project in words, not a property.
The panel's copy of an asset's import settings, which collects edits until Apply or Revert.
A test that reads source files as text and fails on a pattern that a rule forbids.
A file in .github/workflows/ that names the events that start it and holds jobs of steps.
What a CMake target hands to the targets that link it: include folders, definitions and links; the keywords PUBLIC, PRIVATE and INTERFACE say who receives them.
The six questions (correctness, tests, style, portability, documentation, commit hygiene) asked of the complete staged diff before every commit.
A count of which lines of code ran during the tests, as a percentage.
Checking that a project uses every entry of the engine's registries, by walking the registries.
A test that sometimes passes and sometimes fails on the same code.
Any branch whose name starts with ci/, which triggers the same checks as the main branch.
A tree of condition and action nodes that an update evaluates from the root downward, one pass per tick.
A rule that turns an agent's situation into a desired velocity.
Convex polygons that cover the walkable floor, searched as a graph.
A decision model that scores every action and runs the best.
A decision model that searches a chain of actions from the current facts to a goal.
A ray from an agent to a target that reaches the target before anything else.
Rules that let agents on their own routes step around each other without a new search.
A character that no person controls and that decides and acts by code.
The time a message needs to travel from one machine to another; its round trip is the round-trip time.
The share of messages that never arrive.
The change of the latency from one message to the next.
Later messages of a stream waiting for an earlier one that was lost.
One fixed step of the simulation counted as a number; the tick rate is the number of ticks a second.
The one simulation that decides what is true for a piece of state.
A separate message that carries its own boundaries and may be lost, copied or reordered.
A way to play over a network in which machines send only inputs and run the same deterministic steps.
Guessing the remote input, running on, and restoring and replaying when the real input differs.
The state of the game at one tick, sent by a server.
Drawing a remote object between the two snapshots that surround a time in the past.
Applying the local player's inputs at once, with the server's movement code.
Taking the server's state as the truth and replaying the inputs it has not applied.
The server moving targets back to the time the shooter saw before it tests a hit.
Sending only what changed since a state the receiver already has.
Sending each player only the objects that matter to that player.
Ways to open a direct connection between machines that sit behind network address translation (NAT).
A server that passes messages between two machines that cannot reach each other directly.
A texture projected onto the surfaces inside a box.
A scene merged into a running scene by an additive load, tracked so that the running scene can remove exactly its entities later.
Loading a scene into a scene that is already running, next to what it holds, instead of replacing it.
